sources.title: Turan
sources.note: Specialist account of Turan as a shifting Iranian epic, geographic, and historical term rather than a nineteenth-century state.

sources.title: Iranian traditional history
sources.note: Explains the epic Iran and Turan opposition and the later mistaken equation of Turanians with all Turks.

sources.title: The Russian Conquest of Central Asia
sources.note: Academic history of Russian imperial expansion, warfare, diplomacy, and uneven local outcomes.

sources.title: Central Asia: Russia’s Near Abroad or Crossroads of Asia?
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis of conquest, regional connections, later borders, and continuing societies.

sources.title: The winter invasion of Khiva, 1839 to 1841
sources.note: Academic chapter on Perovskii’s failed winter invasion, logistics, dependence on camels, and the turn toward frontier forts.

sources.title: History of the Kokand Khanate
sources.note: Official Uzbekistan history of Kokand rulers, irrigation, diplomacy, conflict, and the 1842 crisis.

sources.title: The numismatic collection of the Kokand State Museum-Reserve
sources.note: Official museum account of Kokand rulers, coin legends, exchange value, and abolition in 1876.

sources.title: Poetic coin legends of nineteenth-century Khoqand
sources.note: Scholarly catalogue with original Persian legends, transliteration, translation, metal, mint, ruler, and date.

sources.title: Kokand diplomatic letters to the Ottoman state
sources.note: Academic conference volume describing nineteenth-century Kokand rulers and diplomatic missions.

sources.title: Khujand
sources.note: Specialist city history covering disputed Kokand-Bukhara frontier status and Russian capture in 1866.

sources.title: Russian Central Asia, 1867 to 1917
sources.note: Academic study of colonial rule, oasis institutions, clan systems, markets, governance, and infrastructure.

sources.title: Identities, Communities, and Nations in Central Asia
sources.note: University paper on layered locality, genealogy, religion, language, lifeway, and later nation making.

sources.title: Categories of identity in late nineteenth-century Central Asia
sources.note: Institute of History review of religious, tribal, regional, linguistic, class, and ethnic categories.

sources.title: Foreword of the Turkestan Album
sources.note: Primary Russian imperial statement of the album’s archaeological, ethnographic, industrial, and conquest purposes.

sources.title: Turkestan Album archaeological part
sources.note: Library guide to 1871 to 1872 photographs, plans, monuments, inscriptions, and Samarkand architecture.

sources.title: Turkestan Album ethnographic part
sources.note: Primary 1871 to 1872 imperial photograph album with 491 portraits and daily-life scenes.

sources.title: Turkestan Album trades part
sources.note: Library guide to exact-period photographs of textiles, metal, timber, leather, farming, baking, and pottery.

sources.title: Court of the qazi: clerks
sources.note: Exact-period albumen photograph and caption showing qazi court clerks in Russian-occupied Central Asia.

sources.title: Central Asian women’s clothing: kurte
sources.note: Exact-period album photograph of two women, robes, braids, and adornment, with colonial-source limits.

sources.title: Itchan Kala
sources.note: UNESCO account of Khiva’s houses, courtyards, markets, caravanserais, mosques, madrasas, and nineteenth-century building.

sources.title: Itchan Kala monument inventory
sources.note: Official inventory recording Khiva’s well, bathhouse, markets, madrasas, houses, and public structures.

sources.title: Historic Centre of Bukhara
sources.note: UNESCO urban history of Bukhara’s fabric, monuments, trade routes, neighborhoods, and architecture.

sources.title: The failure of the Syr-Darya line as a frontier, 1841 to 1863
sources.note: Academic chapter on Raim, Aq Masjid, forts, logistics, Kazakh pastoralists, Bukharan grain traders, and the contested frontier.

sources.title: Eugene Schuyler, Turkistan, volume I
sources.note: Digitized 1876 outsider travel account used critically for markets, water, streets, schools, food, and colonial observation.

sources.title: Educating Muslim Intellectuals in nineteenth-century Central Asia
sources.note: Academic study of Bukharan and Persianate madrasa networks, Arabic learning, Persian high culture, and Turkic forms.

sources.title: Traditional education in nineteenth-century Fergana
sources.note: Scholarly study of maktab starting ages, long study, religious teaching, Persian learning, and source bias.

sources.title: Muslim Women of the Fergana Valley
sources.note: Critical edition of a near-endpoint ethnography based on local-language observation of women’s lives from birth to death.

sources.title: Baku to Bukhara
sources.note: Museum account of nineteenth-century domestic embroidery made at home by women and girls for household use.

sources.title: Silk Roads applied arts, textiles and carpets
sources.note: UNESCO history of suzani design, women’s and girls’ work, trousseaux, cotton grounds, and household uses.

sources.title: Hair or plait ornament
sources.note: Museum object record for nineteenth-century Central Asian jewelry materials and Bukhara, Khiva, Samarkand, and Kokand trade.

sources.title: Bukhara ikat ensemble
sources.note: Museum record for a nineteenth-century Bukhara women’s ensemble woven from silk and cotton ikat.

sources.title: Bukhara chapan
sources.note: Museum record for a third-quarter nineteenth-century silk ikat robe with cotton and silk lining.

sources.title: Bukhara woman’s ikat coat
sources.note: Museum record for an 1850 to 1899 woven, padded, braided silk-and-cotton coat.

sources.title: Turkmen tent door hanging
sources.note: Museum account of a portable first-half nineteenth-century Turkmen ensi, tent life, protection, and furnishing.

sources.title: Turkmen textiles
sources.note: Smithsonian account of exact-period portable furnishings woven by women for domestic use and bazaar income.

sources.title: Indigenous medical systems in nineteenth-century Central Asia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Greco-Islamic medicine, family transmission, books, multilingual learning, and natural substances.

sources.title: Diseases and treatments in nineteenth-century Turkestan travel accounts
sources.note: History-of-medicine review of traveler evidence, herbal and non-herbal remedies, epidemics, and outsider bias.

sources.title: Medical institutions in the city of Turkistan
sources.note: Historical study of post-1864 infirmaries, outpatient care, finances, local healing, and colonial medicine.

sources.title: Quarantines and copper amulets in the Kazakh steppe
sources.note: Social history of nineteenth-century cholera campaigns, quarantine, resistance, and conflicting imperial programs.

sources.title: Wormwood, nomads’ rights, and capitalism in Russian Turkestan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of pastoral rights, medicinal wormwood, trade, veterinary use, and early colonial extraction.

sources.title: Beyond the Bazaars: geographies of the slave trade in Central Asia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of coercive mobility, Persian captives, markets, routes, and Russian abolition claims.

sources.title: Muslim elites of nineteenth-century Khorezm
sources.note: Historical Ethnology study of Khivan elites and the 1874 establishment of a local lithographic press.

sources.title: Campaigning on the Oxus and the fall of Khiva
sources.note: Smithsonian catalogue record for the exact-period 1874 primary account of the Khiva campaign and Turkmen violence.

sources.title: Central Asian historiography
sources.note: Specialist review of Persian and Chagatai historical writing, manuscripts, oral information, and court production.

sources.title: Central Asia: geographical survey
sources.note: Scholarly overview of shifting regional definitions, river basins, deserts, steppes, mountains, and aridity.

sources.title: Central Asia in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
sources.note: Specialist political history of the khanates, the failed Khiva expedition, Russian frontier forts, and conquest through 1868.

sources.title: The fall of Khiva, 1872 to 1873
sources.note: Academic chapter on the 1873 campaign, Khiva’s constrained ruler, and the massacre of Yomut Turkmen communities.

proposedOverrides.name: Turan
proposedOverrides.summary: A careful regional guide to distinct Central Asian communities hidden beneath the atlas’s shifting 1815 to 1878 “Turan” umbrella.
